source.title: Initial boundary value problem for Korteweg-de Vries equation: a review and open problems

accepted.question_text: For the Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem on a finite interval, with equation u_t + u_x + u_{xxx} + u u_x = 0 on 0 < x < L and t > 0, initial data u(x,0)=φ(x), and general boundary conditions B_k u = h, determine whether the problem is globally well-posed in the Sobolev space H^s(0,L) for some s ≥ 0. Equivalently, determine whether solutions can blow up in H^s(0,L) in finite time, and in particular whether one can prove a global a priori L^2(0,L) bound for all times.
accepted.context_brief: Global well-posedness and blow-up for finite-interval KdV IBVP

evidence.quote: • Is the IBVP (4.18) globally well-posed in the space H s (0, L) for some s ≥ 0 or equivalently, does any solution of the IBVP (4.18) blow up in the some space H s (0, L) in finite time?

Consequently, it suffices to establish a global a priori L2 (0, L) estimate sup ku(·,t)kL2 (0,L) < +∞, 0≤t<∞ for solutions of the IBVP (4.18) in order to obtain the global well-posedness of the IBVP (4.18) in the space H s (0, L) for any s ≥ 0.

accepted.question_text: For the same finite-interval Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem u_t + u_x + u_{xxx} + u u_x = 0 with initial data u(x,0)=φ(x) and general boundary conditions B_k u = h on 0 < x < L, determine whether the problem is well-posed in H^s(0,L) for some regularity level s ≤ -1. The paper states that local well-posedness is known for s ≥ 0 and can be extended to -1 < s ≤ 0, but the regime s ≤ -1 remains unresolved, with the authors conjecturing ill-posedness for every s < -1.
accepted.context_brief: Low-regularity well-posedness threshold for finite-interval KdV IBVP

evidence.quote: • Is the IBVP well-posed in the space H s (0, L) for some s ≤ −1?
Theorem G ensures that the IBVP (4.18) is locally well-posed in the space H s (0, L) for any s ≥ 0. Theorem G can also be extended to the case of −1 < s ≤ 0 using the same approach developed in [8].
We conjecture that the IBVP (4.18) is ill-posed in the space H s (0, L) for any s < −1.

accepted.question_text: For the pure initial value problem for the Korteweg-de Vries equation on the whole line, u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0 with x,t ∈ R and initial data u(x,0)=φ(x), determine whether the problem is well-posed in H^s(R) for some s < -3/4. The paper notes well-posedness for s ≥ -3/4 and conditional ill-posedness below that threshold in the sense that the solution map is not uniformly continuous, but says the existence of a well-posed theory below s = -3/4 is still open.
accepted.context_brief: Subcritical low-regularity KdV IVP on the line

evidence.quote: Whether the IVP (4.20) is well-posed in the space H s (R) for any s < − 34 or the IVP (4.21) is well-posed in the space H s (T) for any s < −1 is still an open question.

accepted.question_text: For the periodic initial value problem for the Korteweg-de Vries equation, u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0 with x ∈ T, t ∈ R, and initial data u(x,0)=φ(x), determine whether the problem is well-posed in H^s(T) for some s < -1. The paper notes well-posedness for s ≥ -1, and says the lower-regularity regime below -1 remains open.

evidence.quote: Whether the IVP (4.20) is well-posed in the space H s (R) for any s < − 34 or the IVP (4.21) is well-posed in the space H s (T) for any s < −1 is still an open question.

accepted.question_text: Consider the nonlinear finite-interval Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem u_t + u u_x + u_{xxx} = 0 on 0 < x < L with initial data u(x,0)=φ(x) and boundary conditions u(0,t)=0, u(L,t)=0, and u_x(0,t)=u_x(L,t). The associated linear problem is known to be well-posed forward and backward in time, but it remains open whether this nonlinear problem is well-posed in H^s(0,L) for any Sobolev exponent s.
accepted.context_brief: Well-posedness of nonlinear KdV with matched derivative boundary data

evidence.quote: However, the following problem is still unknown:
• Is the nonlinear IBVP (4.23) well-posed in the space H s (0, L) for some s ?

accepted.question_text: For the finite-interval Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem u_t + u_x + u_{xxx} + u u_x = 0 with initial data u(x,0)=φ(x) and general boundary conditions B_k u = h, determine whether the system is controllable under completely general boundary conditions, beyond the specific boundary-control configurations B_{1,0}, B_{2,0}, and B_{4,0} discussed in the paper.

evidence.quote: Thus, with respect of the control issue, a natural and interesting open problem arises here:
• Is the IBVP (4.18), with general boundary condition, controllable?
